messages:
incident-bot: [AUTOPAGE] PagerDuty alert fired for service: node.kubelet.heartbeat-missed on host gpu-rt-17 (region: us-west2). Severity: P1. Requesting immediate ack and triage. https://pagerduty.example/incident/PD12345 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Incident PD12345 - triggered at 2026-03-15T07:12:57Z. Status: needs-ack. Assigned to oncall-sre.
alex.sre: acked via PD and joining. seeing node unresponsive to kubelet heartbeat probe. checking metrics now.
james.devops: grabbing serial console, pulling kernel logs. If it's kernel oops we'll need to isolate.
elaine.ops: pinging node from rack mgmt, BMC reachable. serial is attaching.
alex.sre: quick impact check — running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-rt-17` to see affected workloads.
alex.sre: output: ```
NAME                                 READY  STATUS   RESTARTS AGE   NODE
model-runner-7f8d9                  1/1    Running  0      12d  gpu-rt-17
batch-render-5c6b2                   0/1    Error    3      3h   gpu-rt-17
customer-a-infer-0                   0/1    CrashLoopBackOff  5  22m  gpu-rt-17
```
alex.sre: customer-a is seeing 502s on inference calls per CS slack ping.
anna.cs: confirmation: customer-A reporting degraded responses starting ~07:10 UTC, ticket #INC-8812. They see timeouts then 502s.
james.devops: serial log shows repeated `kworker` OOPS followed by `kmsg: kernel panic - not syncing`. Looks like a kernel oops loop. snippet: ```
[ 1234.567890] NMI: Watchdog detected hard LOCKUP on CPU 3
[ 1234.568012] kernel panic - not syncing: Attn: GPU fault XID 79
[ 1234.568200] ---[ end trace 3d2b9c4a ]---
```
james.devops: also seeing NVMe errors immediately before panic, might be IO related, collecting `dmesg` & `smartctl`.
elaine.ops: I'll cordon the node to prevent new pods scheduling: `kubectl cordon gpu-rt-17` then start evicting non-critical jobs.
alex.sre: agree. make sure we don't evict the model-runner if it's stateful without fallback. we'll route traffic to model-runner replicas elsewhere via routing policy.
elaine.ops: ran `kubectl cordon gpu-rt-17` — node now cordoned. Draining non-prod workloads: `kubectl drain gpu-rt-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` in progress.
deploy-bot: detected drain command; starting canary shift of traffic for `customer-a-infer` to replica set in us-west2-b.
alex.sre: for production impact: 1 dedicated GPU host down, ~3 pods impacted, customer-A degraded but has failover; CS engaged and monitoring. Logging timeline in incident doc.
anna.cs: updating customer ticket: "We've detected a host failure affecting some inference pods. We're draining the node and failing over workloads; will provide ETA after failover completes." :white_check_mark:
james.devops: got full `journalctl -k -b -1` pulled and packing for RMA if HW culprit. attaching snippet to the incident doc.
james.devops: quick mitigation note — trying soft-reboot via BMC after draining to see if node comes back clean, else quarantine for disk/RMA.
alex.sre: also enabling automatic fallback rule in routing: if gpu-rt-17 host unavailable, route requests to `model-runner-spot` pool. patch applied: `rbac: routing -> added fallback for node:gpu-rt-17`
elaine.ops: drain finished. `kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-rt-17` now shows only DaemonSets and kube-proxy.
PagerDuty: PD12345 acknowledged by alex.sre at 2026-03-15T07:14:03Z.
alex.sre: handing off to night-oncall in 35m; will update runbook and add summary. tagging @ops-next for follow-up.
anna.cs: customer notified: they acknowledged the mitigation, will monitor traffic.
james.devops: BMC soft-reboot did not return node to normal — kernel panic repeats on boot. marking host as hardware-failed and initiating RMA. filing infra ticket INFRA-4123.
alex.sre: summary for handoff -> Cause: likely hardware NVMe/GPU fault causing kernel oops -> Impact: single GPU host, few pods evicted, customer-A degraded briefly but routed to fallback -> Mitigation: cordon+drain, route traffic to fallback pool, RMA started -> Next: infra to RMA gpu-rt-17, oncall-next to monitor post-failover customer metrics and remove fallback when stable.
elaine.ops: setting follow-up reminder: `@oncall-next` please check cluster autoscaler behaviour — ensure new capacity spin-up if needed.
alex.sre: adding tags to incident PD12345: `gpu, kernel-panic, rma, customer-impact`
anna.cs: closing initial customer alert: "Failover applied, we're monitoring, next update in 30m."
alex.sre: handing over live thread to @oncall-next. I'm out in 30. ack/close PD when stable. :handshake:
